A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sequential Boltzmann Generators study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and sampling experiments on alanine peptides and Chignolin, including quantitative comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original peptide-sampling experiments, including AIS/SMC comparisons, revised Chignolin results, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Equation (5) changes the quadratic centroid term from negative to positive, revising the specified center-of-mass correction used in reweighting. The TarFlow backbone and annealed Langevin/SMC procedure remain; AIS was already described in v1.

E1.justification: The molecular systems remain the same, but the Chignolin scenario is substantially replaced. v1 uses an external explicit-solvent trajectory against an implicit-solvent target; v2 generates a 4.5-microsecond implicit-solvent trajectory using the target configuration (Appendix D). This removes the solvent-transfer scenario and changes the data environment of the largest-system demonstration.

E2.justification: ECNF is removed from trialanine/tetrapeptide comparisons and chirality Table 8, while remaining in the alanine-dipeptide comparison. The reweighting ablation adds ECNF++ proposal/SNIS controls, and Figure 13 adds SE(3)-EACF. Comparator participation changes without introducing a new external baseline family.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the main 10k/100k SMC comparisons with 10k AIS/SMC comparisons and omits post-resampling SMC ESS. E-W1 becomes E-W2, the torus cost changes from modulo pi to wrapped 2-pi differences, and TICA-W2 is added. Reported training/validation durations change from 100/20 ps to 1/0.2 microseconds, with smaller test subsets. Model selection, chirality filtering, Chignolin model size and annealing settings, and timing hardware also change.

E4.justification: The existing center-of-mass, clipping, sample-count, timestep, and chirality analyses largely remain. The reweighting ablation gains ECNF++ controls, SBG AIS rows, and TICA diagnostics (v2 Tables 9–10). Conversely, the resampling-threshold sensitivity study in v1 Figure 20 is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.1 newly states that entries with ± represent three independently trained and sampled models; v1 reports ± without specifying this count. v2 also supplies uncertainty for previously single-valued hexa-alanine SBG results. This establishes expanded reporting, not necessarily an increased run budget.

E6.justification: Main and appendix scores are extensively replaced or extended. For example, v1 Table 2 favors SBG@100k over ECNF++ on T-W2 (0.226 versus 0.293), whereas v2 favors ECNF++ (0.189 versus AIS 0.418 and SMC 0.430). v2 adds AIS/TICA results and Chignolin E-W2 values of 12.046 for SNIS and 3.571 for SMC. Revised metrics and settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting cross-version gains.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and Appendix B.1 are replaced: v1 asserts preservation of the mean-free marginal under invariant centroid noise; v2 claims asymptotic ESS improvement under Gaussian-noise and factorization assumptions, with a new weight-moment argument. Equation (5) and the mathematical definition of the torus cost also change. The other thresholding and Itô arguments are substantially retained.

C1.justification: The central TarFlow-plus-annealing contributions and peptide-scaling claims remain. The introduction reframes the theoretical contribution from an automatic optimal-threshold scheme toward a novel centroid-energy adjustment and thresholding-bias analysis. The broad abstract claim of state-of-the-art performance across all metrics is retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds a likelihood-estimation explanation for ECNF++ failures and qualifies SMC's advantage over SNIS as dependent on proposal overlap. Appendix F.3 develops the energy-versus-macrostructure tradeoff already visible in v1. Chignolin's earlier mismatch and incomplete-sampling caveats disappear alongside the changed scenario; the costly-CNF limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release link, specifies centroid-noise standard deviation as 1/sqrt(n), and documents POT, heavy-atom TICA processing, and the new Chignolin simulation. It removes the ECNF++ normalization recipe and explicit multinomial/stratified resampling choices. Revised ECNF++ weight-decay documentation conflicts internally: 10^-4 in the prose versus 10^-2 in Table 7.

R1.justification: Section 5 gains an extensive amortized-sampling discussion covering diffusion samplers, flow-assisted MCMC, and ODE bridges, including Arbel et al. (2021), Matthews et al. (2022), and Chen et al. (2025). This substantially broadens the positioning beyond v1's molecular Boltzmann-generator survey. Publication updates to retained references are separate bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and results undergo extensive rewriting. Section 4.1 gains dataset-specific discussions and clearer AIS/SMC terminology; related work and metric explanations expand, and Appendix E separates metrics from timings. Author affiliations and running-header text also change.

P2.justification: Energy histograms, runtime plots, Ramachandran plots, and ablation figures are widely redrawn with revised colors, axes, legends, and captions. Tables 2–3 regroup datasets and method variants, while v1 Table 9 becomes v2 Tables 9–10. Figures are extensively rearranged, and the resampling-threshold plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evaluation interpretability through a Chignolin reference simulated under the target setup, clearer AIS/SMC comparisons, and removal of post-resampling SMC ESS. Run-count disclosure, code information, and TICA comparisons add useful support. Gains are limited by unexplained main/appendix SBG score differences, retained Table 8 values despite revised evaluation, conflicting weight-decay settings, and an across-metrics superiority claim contradicted by Table 2.
